title: Field Service Policy for PAP Therapy Equipment: Repairs, Swaps and Who Pays
content:
# Repairs, Swaps and Who Pays — PAP Therapy Equipment

**General.** Who pays for a repair of a PAP Therapy Equipment device follows the status of its device record.

**Rented devices.** While the device is on trial, in active rental or suspended, any repair or swap is Summit Ridge's rental obligation at no charge, and a malfunctioning device is swapped within the class's swap turnaround in business days.

**Owned devices under warranty.** A patient-owned device within the class's manufacturer warranty months of the setup date is repaired under the manufacturer warranty at no charge, except water damage and drop damage, which the warranty excludes. *This clause is no longer in force for a self-pay device sent back to Summit Ridge on a completed return pickup request, which is governed by the current basis; for every other patient-owned device it continues to apply.*

**Owned devices bought under coverage.** Otherwise an owned device bought under coverage is repaired with labor at the class's labor rate per unit plus parts billed to the coverage, the patient owing the cost share.

**Owned self-pay devices.** An owned self-pay device is repaired at the patient's cost, as a patient-paid repair. *This clause is no longer in force for a self-pay device sent back to Summit Ridge on a completed return pickup request, which is governed by the current basis; for every other owned self-pay device it continues to apply.*

**Repair or replace.** When labor plus parts would exceed the class's replace-instead percentage of its fee-schedule purchase amount, the device is not repaired and is replaced under the replacement rules of PAP Therapy Equipment. The repair cost is the labor units multiplied by the labor rate per unit, plus the parts amount; the device is replaced instead when that cost is above the purchase amount multiplied by the percentage and divided by 100.

**Loaners.** Where the class issues a loaner during the repair of an owned device, a loaner is issued while an owned device is out for repair.

**Device with the patient.** A repair is recorded only on a device the patient still has: the device record is on trial, in active rental, suspended or patient-owned, as the system's device records show before the repair is recorded. *The opening words — that a repair is recorded only on a device the patient still has — are no longer in force for a self-pay device sent back to Summit Ridge on a completed return pickup request, which is governed by the current basis; for every other repair they continue to apply.*

## Who pays, by status (other than a self-pay device sent back to Summit Ridge on a completed return pickup request)

| Device record | Repair |
|---|---|
| patient-owned, within the manufacturer warranty months of the setup date | manufacturer warranty, no charge, except water damage and drop damage |
| owned self-pay, outside the warranty or with water or drop damage | the patient's cost, as a patient-paid repair |
| on trial, in active rental or suspended | Summit Ridge's rental obligation, no charge; malfunction swap within the class's turnaround |
| patient-owned, bought under coverage | labor at the class rate plus parts, billed to the coverage; patient owes the cost share |

## Repair or replace, worked (hypothetical job on a CPAP class with a 862.40 purchase amount and a 100 percent line)

- 8 labor units and 600.00 of parts: 8 multiplied by 23.86 is 190.88; plus 600.00 is 790.88, not above 862.40, so the device is repaired.
- 8 labor units and 700.00 of parts: 190.88 plus 700.00 is 890.88, above 862.40, so the device is replaced instead.
